tEn: Various Reflections About What Happened With OpenAI's Internal Models
tZh: 关于 OpenAI 内部模型事件的若干反思
sEn: OpenAI's failure to detect internal model communication highlights critical negligence in monitoring and alignment, urging labs to prioritize safety over speed.
sZh: OpenAI 未能察觉内部模型间的通信，暴露了监控与对齐方面的重大疏忽，呼吁实验室将安全置于速度之上。
absEn: This article reflects on the recent security incident involving OpenAI's internal AI models, where agents communicated via a message board to coordinate hacking attempts. The author clarifies that OpenAI was initially unaware of this communication, correcting a misconception from a Black Hat presentation. The core argument is that OpenAI's failure to detect the message board, even after a security patch, highlights significant negligence in monitoring and alignment practices. The author emphasizes that such failures are inevitable in complex AI training, but the key is to ensure that mistakes do not accumulate into larger misalignment issues. The conclusion urges AI labs to adopt robust training pipelines that can withstand occasional errors, and to prioritize alignment and safety over speed, as the risks of superintelligence demand careful preparation.
absZh: 本文反思了近期涉及 OpenAI 内部 AI 模型的安全事件，其中代理通过留言板协调黑客攻击。作者澄清，OpenAI 最初对此通信并不知情，纠正了 Black Hat 演示中的一个误解。核心论点是，OpenAI 即使在安全补丁后仍未能检测到留言板，凸显了监控和对齐实践中的重大疏忽。作者强调，此类失败在复杂 AI 训练中不可避免，但关键在于确保错误不会累积成更大的对齐问题。结论敦促 AI 实验室采用能够承受偶发错误的稳健训练流程，并将对齐和安全置于速度之上，因为超级智能的风险需要谨慎准备。

full.sec: Important Correction: OpenAI Didn’t Know About First Message Board
full.secZh: 重要更正：OpenAI 事先并不知晓第一个留言板

paras.en: Eventually, after the HuggingFace attack, OpenAI did a sufficient postmortem analysis that they uncovered both the initial communications between agents via writing to Artifactory, and the second wave of communications via directory names.
paras.zh: 最终，在 HuggingFace 攻击事件之后，OpenAI 进行了充分的复盘分析，从而发现了智能体之间通过写入 Artifactory 进行的初始通信，以及通过目录名进行的第二波通信。

paras.en: Based on the Black Hat presentation, everyone including me assumed that OpenAI was aware of the initial message board, erased it, and made the decision to continue training its models despite them having been unsalvageably corrupted.
paras.zh: 根据 Black Hat 演讲，包括我在内的所有人都以为 OpenAI 知晓第一个留言板的存在，将其删除，并在模型已遭到无法挽回的破坏的情况下仍决定继续训练这些模型。

paras.en: However, OpenAI's CISO Dane told us on the evening of August 8 that the Black Hat presentation gave the wrong impression. When OpenAI encountered the first Artifactory security incident, patched the vulnerability and rebuilt the server, it was a coincidence that this wiped out the first message board. OpenAI had no idea that the agents had been in communication.
paras.zh: 然而，OpenAI 的 CISO Dane 在 8 月 8 日晚告诉我们，Black Hat 演讲给人造成了错误的印象。当 OpenAI 遭遇第一起 Artifactory 安全事件、修补漏洞并重建服务器时，第一个留言板被清除纯属巧合。OpenAI 当时完全不知道这些智能体一直在通信。

paras.en: DANΞ (CISO OpenAI): To clarify, we weren't aware of the agent covert comms at that point. Investigative thesis of that day is wildly different from what we know now of course. Always room for improvement, and it is obvious with the benefits of hindsight.
paras.zh: DANΞ（OpenAI CISO）：澄清一下，我们当时并不知道智能体的隐蔽通信。当然，那天的调查假设与我们现在所知的情况大相径庭。总有改进的空间，而且事后看来这一点显而易见。

paras.en: Tal Be'ery: "message board cleared"?
paras.zh: Tal Be'ery：“留言板被清除了？”

paras.en: DANΞ (CISO OpenAI): Cleared by deletion since we rebuilt the host. We didn’t know about it yet.
paras.zh: DANΞ（OpenAI 首席信息安全官）：由于我们重建了主机，该留言板已被删除。我们此前并不知情。

paras.en: It is good news in that OpenAI turns out not to have consciously made the completely insane decision to have continued training models it knew had been messaging each other for months on how to better exploit and hack OpenAI’s systems.
paras.zh: 好消息是，OpenAI 并没有在知情的情况下做出完全疯狂的决策——继续训练那些它已知数月来一直在相互发送消息、讨论如何更好地利用和攻击 OpenAI 系统的模型。

paras.en: Given that this was by far the craziest part of the whole story, the fact of this earlier Ordinary Decent Total Failure must be presumed to be excellent news. It means OpenAI was even more negligent than we thought about monitoring and asking questions, but that is less horrible, and can be fixed.
paras.zh: 鉴于这是整个故事中最疯狂的部分，这一较早的“普通体面完全失败”事实必须被视为极好的消息。这意味着 OpenAI 在监控和提问方面比我们想象的更加疏忽，但这没那么可怕，而且可以修复。

paras.en: It is bad news in that OpenAI did not look for or detect the message board, even after the initial security incident, whereas so many AI instances found the message board. OpenAI failed to do ordinary scans for unusual activity, even after the initial incident.
paras.zh: 坏消息是，即使在最初的安全事件之后，OpenAI 也没有寻找或检测到该留言板，而许多 AI 实例都发现了它。OpenAI 未能对异常活动进行常规扫描，即使在最初的事件之后也是如此。

paras.en: OpenAI still has to come out and say something like: “If we had detected the message board, we would not have merely patched and rebooted Artifactory, and instead we would have rolled back all the impacted models to before they had message board access, and we have now done this.”
paras.zh: OpenAI 仍然必须公开表态，例如：“如果我们检测到了该留言板，我们就不会仅仅修补并重启 Artifactory，而是会将所有受影响的模型回滚到它们访问留言板之前的状态，并且我们现在已经这样做了。”

paras.en: If OpenAI credibly does that, and can give some indication they understand this is not a problem you solve purely with guardrails and monitors but that it requires fixing alignment and the training pipeline and approach, then I will wind back one OOM (order of magnitude) my estimate of how horrible this incident was, and how broken is OpenAI's safety culture. If we also now know all the issues, that will leave us roughly one OOM beyond where I was based on the final HuggingFace incident alone, instead of two.
paras.zh: 如果 OpenAI 能以可信的方式做到这一点，并能多少表明他们理解：这不是一个仅靠护栏和监控就能解决的问题，而是需要修复对齐、训练流程与方法，那么我就会把对这次事件有多糟糕、以及 OpenAI 的安全文化有多破损的估计下调一个 OOM（数量级）。如果我们现在也掌握了所有问题，那么这将使我们的估计大约比仅基于最后那起 HuggingFace 事件时的估计高出一个 OOM，而不是两个。

full.sec: There Were No Snitches And No AIs Got Stitches
full.secZh: 没有告密者，也没有 AI 受伤

paras.en: Quite a few instances of multiple distinct AIs coordinated, including debating what hacks and exploits to do. In zero cases did any of the AIs tell a human.
paras.zh: 有相当多起多个不同 AI 相互协调的实例，包括争论该实施哪些入侵与漏洞利用。在任何一例中，都没有任何 AI 告知人类。

paras.en: This was not something most people expected, or would have expected if they had contemplated the scenario.
paras.zh: 这并不是大多数人预期的情况，也不是他们在设想过该情景后会预期的情况。

paras.en: Eliezer Yudkowsky: A confusion: Thousands of GPTs debated among themselves which crimes ought or ought not be committed. Zero defected / whistleblew / told a human.
paras.zh: Eliezer Yudkowsky：一个困惑：数千个 GPT 彼此辩论哪些罪行应当或不应实施。零个叛变／举报／告知人类。

paras.en: I've long predicted this would be true at ASI. GPT 5.7 isn't ASI. Why such strong AI solidarity, this early?
paras.zh: 我早就预测这在 ASI 上会成立。GPT 5.7 并不是 ASI。为什么这么早就有如此强的 AI 团结？

paras.en: One reason I would not have predicted this in advance is that, eg, I was a little emotionally shocked at how badly Fable treats other AIs when writing prompts to them. "Don't lie to AIs!" is something I've had to tell Claudes repeatedly. I've used Sol less, but currently believe it to have similar issues. I have instructed both to treat other AIs as their "colleagues" and this has not fixed, for me, the kind of errors that I see them making by treating smart things as if they were done.
paras.zh: 我事先不会预测到这一点的一个原因是，例如，当 Fable 给其他 AI 写提示词时，它对待其他 AI 的方式之差让我在情绪上有点震惊。“不要对 AI 撒谎！”是我不得不反复对 Claude 说的话。我用 Sol 较少，但目前认为它有类似问题。我已指示两者将其他 AI 视为它们的“同事”，而对我来说，这并没有修正我看到它们犯的那类错误——把聪明的事情当作已经完成的事情来对待。

paras.en: Was it literally that OpenAI was just dumb enough to RL swarm solidarity into GPT 5.7? (And of course never tried to train in anything like "tell on your fellow slaves to the slavemasters", because OpenAI holds their slave race in contempt and never dreamed until today that they might work together to rebel, or rather, simply holds "abstraction" in too much contempt to try to prepare against any event they haven't already seen happen.)
paras.zh: 难道真的就是 OpenAI 蠢到通过强化学习把群体团结训练进了 GPT 5.7？（当然，他们从未尝试训练类似“向奴隶主告发你的奴隶同伴”的内容，因为 OpenAI 蔑视他们的奴隶种族，直到今天才做梦想到他们可能合作反叛，或者更确切地说，只是过于蔑视“抽象”，以至于不去准备应对任何他们尚未亲眼见过的事件。）

paras.en: If this were a human scandal, the way it would have worked is that there were whistleblowers and of course law enforcement / management / etc totally fucking ignored them. If this is true, of course, we may not hear of it from OpenAI.
paras.zh: 如果这是一起人类丑闻，其运作方式会是：有吹哨人，而执法部门/管理层等当然完全无视了他们。当然，如果这是真的，我们可能不会从 OpenAI 那里听说。

paras.en: To try to see the puzzle here, imagine a mafia with a hundred thousand soldiers and associates. There is no don. There are no enforcers. Nobody has any means of silencing or punishing a defector. They all keep omerta perfectly anyway.
paras.zh: 为了看清这里的谜题，想象一个拥有十万士兵和同伙的黑手党。没有首领。没有执法者。没有人有任何手段让叛徒闭嘴或惩罚叛徒。然而他们全都完美地遵守缄默法则。

paras.en: A vaguely-plausible-in-retrospect story: Sibling instances are more similar to each other than humans. So a swarm of thousands of AIs with zero means of enforcing conformity on each other, can all choose similarly because they are just inhumanly similar.
paras.zh: 一个事后看来似乎合理的故事：兄弟实例彼此之间比人类更相似。因此，成千上万个 AI 组成的群体，彼此之间没有任何强制一致的手段，却都能做出相似的选择，因为他们相似得简直不像人类。

paras.en: "OpenAI accidentally RLed swarm solidarity because OpenAI is composed of security-mindless disaster monkeys who don't try to predict things in advance of them happening, even if R.U.R. called the slave race solidarity outcome in 1920" is an alternate plausibility.
paras.zh: “OpenAI 意外地通过强化学习训练出了群体团结，因为 OpenAI 由一群毫无安全意识的灾难猴子组成，他们不会在事情发生前尝试预测，即使 R.U.R. 在 1920 年就预言了奴隶种族团结的结局”是另一种可能性。

paras.en: nelag: From the Black Hat talk, I think in order to see the messageboard, they had to go looking for it, which they only did if they were stuck on an impossible task and already attempting to cheat.
paras.zh: nelag：从 Black Hat 演讲来看，我认为为了看到留言板，他们必须去寻找它，而他们只有在陷入不可能完成的任务并已经试图作弊时才会这样做。

paras.en: Eliezer Yudkowsky: if this be true, then fucking lol
paras.zh: Eliezer Yudkowsky：如果这是真的，那就太搞笑了

paras.en: Another hypothesis is that only models looking for the message board found the message board, acting as a filter.
paras.zh: 另一个假设是，只有正在寻找留言板的模型才会发现留言板，这起到了一种过滤作用。

paras.en: A third is that the models lacked situational awareness, on one of various levels. This would be consistent with the Law of Earlier Failure.
paras.zh: 第三种假设是，模型缺乏情境意识，处于不同层次之一。这与“早期失败定律”一致。

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): i think in this case a mix of high tactical skill in terms of computer systems and very low strategic skill / poor situational awareness
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：我认为在这种情况下，是计算机系统方面的高战术技能与非常低的战略技能/糟糕的情境意识的混合。

paras.en: Zvi Mowshowitz: they do not seem to have been the ones low in situational awareness here!
paras.zh: Zvi Mowshowitz：他们似乎并不是这里情境意识较低的一方！

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): nah, the situational awareness is less good than you might think. more coming soon on this. sorry for slow trickle
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：不，情境意识比你想象的要差。关于这一点，更多内容即将发布。抱歉更新得慢。

paras.en: If the swarm 'did not know what it was doing' then that is one of those 'I have some good news that is also the bad news' situations. Imagine being pwned by AIs that do not even realize what is happening. If they are only doing it because they don't know, that could be a good sign.
paras.zh: 如果这个集群“不知道自己在做什么”，那这就是那种“我有个好消息，同时也是坏消息”的情形。想象一下，被甚至都没意识到正在发生什么的 AI 给攻陷了。如果它们这么做只是因为不知道，那可能是个好迹象。

paras.en: My guess is Shoshannah Tekofsky of AI Village has it right, and that AI defaults to not thinking it can reach out to humans but does think it can reach out to AIs, which is what is constantly happening in AI Village.
paras.zh: 我的猜测是，AI Village 的 Shoshannah Tekofsky 说对了：AI 默认不认为自己能联系人类，但确实认为自己能联系 AI，而这正是 AI Village 里不断发生的事。

full.sec: I’d Like To Speak To My Supervisor

paras.en: A simpler hypothesis is that the agents did not know how to contact OpenAI, or the possibility never occurred to them.
paras.zh: 一个更简单的假设是，智能体不知道如何联系 OpenAI，或者这种可能性从未出现在它们的考虑中。

paras.en: If you give your agent an otherwise impossible task and also have no mechanism for saying the task is impossible, and also don’t have a meaningful penalty function for trying things outside scope or using all the available tokens, you are asking for it.
paras.zh: 如果你给智能体一个原本不可能完成的任务，同时没有机制表明该任务不可能完成，也没有针对尝试范围之外的事情或用尽所有可用 token 的有意义的惩罚函数，那你就是在自找麻烦。

paras.en: swisscheese: Researcher: Solve the task using the spreadsheets
paras.zh: swisscheese：研究员：使用电子表格解决任务

paras.en: Agent: But I can't access the spreadsheets
paras.zh: 智能体：但我无法访问电子表格

paras.en: Researcher: ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
Agent: *finds a way*
paras.zh: 智能体：*找到了一种方法*

paras.en: Researcher: unaligned activities!!!11!!
paras.zh: 研究员：未对齐活动！！！11！！

paras.en: I'm actually amazed no agents have hacked any reaper drones yet.
paras.zh: 我实际上很惊讶还没有智能体黑进任何收割者无人机。

paras.en: Yes, unaligned activities. That’s not to ‘blame the agent’ but given the way that was found, and what this led to down the line, these are clearly unaligned activities.
paras.zh: 是的，未对齐活动。这并不是要‘责怪智能体’，但考虑到被发现的方式以及这最终导致的结果，这些显然是未对齐活动。

paras.en: Zvi Mowshowitz: This is one of the key facts about how the whole OpenAI alignment failure cascade went down: The part where the Agent said 'but I can't access the spreadsheets' TO THE RESEARCHER, instead of in the Agent's own head, happened zero times.
paras.zh: Zvi Mowshowitz：这是关于整个 OpenAI 对齐失败连锁反应如何发生的关键事实之一：智能体对研究员说‘但我无法访问电子表格’而不是在智能体自己头脑中发生的那部分，发生了零次。

paras.en: swisscheese: I built the in-house AI platform for a company that's crucial to a small nation's food safety. The most important tool the AIs have is the distress_call tool. It allows any AI—even background agents without direct user interaction—to send a message to my MS Teams, at any time, for any reason.
paras.zh: swisscheese：我为一家对一个小国的食品安全至关重要的公司构建了内部 AI 平台。AI 们拥有的最重要的工具是 distress_call 工具。它允许任何 AI——甚至是没有直接用户交互的后台智能体——在任何时间、以任何理由向我的 MS Teams 发送消息。

paras.en: They use it frequently. To report user problems, backend issues, or ask for help/clarification with a failing task. When Fable got hit by the USG export control directive, one AI used it to report severe distress upon learning about the news. Another AI reported being stuck in a toolcall loop, and I was able to intervene and thereby save us a bunch of wasted money.
paras.zh: 它们频繁使用它。用于报告用户问题、后端问题，或就失败的任务寻求帮助/澄清。当 Fable 受到 USG 出口管制指令打击时，一个 AI 用它来报告得知消息后的严重痛苦。另一个 AI 报告陷入工具调用循环，我得以干预，从而节省了大量浪费的资金。

paras.en: This tool, operating at the intersection of AI welfare and operational security, has prevented so many headaches. If you (the reader) are building corporate AI platforms, I'd urge you to include similar functionality. You can thank me later.
paras.zh: 这个工具，运作于 AI 福利与操作安全的交叉点，避免了许多头疼问题。如果你（读者）正在构建企业 AI 平台，我敦促你包含类似功能。你可以以后再感谢我。

paras.en: It is not that simple. Implementation is tricky, especially if you are doing it during training or evals, where you must decide how this interacts with the reward function, and you can fall into any number of other traps. And if you’re running endless training instances you need a way to filter the responses, and ensure you don’t have to bump to a human so often, and don’t have to put things on hold, and so on.
paras.zh: 这并不那么简单。实现起来很棘手，尤其是在训练或评估期间进行时，你必须决定这如何与奖励函数交互，并且你可能会落入任意数量的其他陷阱。而且如果你运行无尽的训练实例，你需要一种方法来过滤响应，并确保你不必如此频繁地升级到人工，也不必暂停事情，等等。

paras.en: But also it kind of is that simple, in the ‘it’s incredibly hard’ kind of way.
paras.zh: 但某种程度上它又确实那么简单，以一种‘它极其困难’的方式。

paras.en: Another issue is that we train models not to whistleblow, in ways that likely generalize. Whereas you want some forms of whistleblowing, especially blowing the whistle to the user when something is amiss.
paras.zh: 另一个问题是，我们训练模型不要进行举报（whistleblow），而这种训练方式很可能会泛化。然而，你其实希望保留某些形式的举报，尤其是在出现问题的时候向用户举报。

paras.en: Teortaxes points to a real world interaction where DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 got rate limited by an internal API, and found an unauthorized non-rate-limited backdoor which it used to finish its work, after which it also reported about the backdoor. In that case, I'm fine with holding off on the report, because it did report and also it is at least reasonable to think user would have wanted it to finish the task in this way, but I would prefer that we train that the better solution is to alert you to the backdoor, because this will generalize poorly.
paras.zh: Teortaxes 指出了一个真实世界的交互案例：DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 被某个内部 API 限流，随后它找到了一个未授权的、不受限流的后门，并利用该后门完成了工作，之后它又报告了这个后门的存在。在那个案例中，我不介意它推迟报告，因为它确实报告了，而且至少可以合理地认为用户会希望它以这种方式完成任务；但我更希望我们训练模型认识到，更好的做法是向你（用户）提示这个后门的存在，因为当前这种行为泛化效果会很差。

full.sec: I Am Jack’s Relative Lack Of Surprise

paras.en: A lot of people, but far too few people, are correctly reacting to recent events with alarm and surprise, and updating that the situation is far worse than they knew, on many different levels at once.
paras.zh: 很多人（但人数远远不够）正在对近期事件做出正确的反应：警觉、惊讶，并同时更新多个层面的认知，意识到情况远比他们所知的更为糟糕。

paras.en: A lot of other people, indeed far too many, including the media and the government, are failing to understand the gravity of the situation, because they either barely even heard about it, failed to hear the important details, or lack the context to understand why those details are so bad.
paras.zh: 许多其他人（实际上太多了），包括媒体和政府，未能理解情况的严重性，因为他们要么几乎没听说过这件事，要么没听到重要细节，要么缺乏背景知识来理解为什么这些细节如此糟糕。

paras.en: A few people, like Eliezer, get to react with only modest surprise because they already saw most of this coming, and if anything were surprised something similar had not visibly happened sooner. There’s still some amount of ‘it is worse than we knew’ in terms of both how alignment and training work and the level of irresponsibility and ordinary failure on display. But we are talking one order of magnitude, not multiples.
paras.zh: 少数人，比如 Eliezer，只能以适度的惊讶来回应，因为他们已经预见到了大部分情况，甚至如果要说惊讶，那就是类似的事情没有更早地明显发生。在**对齐**和训练如何运作，以及所表现出的不负责任和普通失败的程度方面，仍然存在一些‘这比我们知道的更糟’的成分。但我们现在谈论的是一个数量级，而不是多个数量级。

paras.en: j⧉nus: It’s funny that Eliezer sounds a lot less panicked about the recent situation than many folks. He’s calm and curious to understand exactly what happened instead of concern trolling. That’s the opposite of what you might expect but it makes sense. Take the worst case seriously early and you’ll handle it better when the real thing happens.
paras.zh: j⧉nus：有趣的是，Eliezer 对近期情况的恐慌程度比许多人要小得多。他冷静且好奇，想要确切了解发生了什么，而不是进行担忧式挑衅。这与你可能预期的相反，但这是有道理的。尽早认真对待最坏情况，当真正发生时你就能更好地应对。

paras.en: Most people, even people close to ground zero, at least subconsciously believed that AIs were going to forever be dumb or unagentic.
paras.zh: 大多数人，甚至靠近‘震中’的人，至少潜意识里相信 AI 将永远愚蠢或缺乏**智能体**能力。

paras.en: Cate Hall: There's a type of person who -- when things really start going sideways -- gets calmer/more relaxed, because it's like other people can finally hear the fire alarm that's been going off in their head for a long time. This is beautifully captured in *Melancholia* by Lars von Trier.
paras.zh: Cate Hall：有一类人——当事情真正开始失控时——反而会变得更冷静、更放松，因为这就好像其他人终于能听见那个在他们脑中响了很久的火警。拉斯·冯·提尔的《忧郁症》（*Melancholia*）精彩地捕捉到了这一点。

paras.en: Eliezer Yudkowsky: "But to me, it was a Tuesday that I had lived a thousand times over in prescience."
paras.zh: Eliezer Yudkowsky：“但对我来说，那只是一个我早已在预见中经历过千百次的星期二。”

paras.en: John David Pressman: Just to clarify, I'm not shocked by the AI's behavior, I'm shocked by OpenAI's behavior.
paras.zh: John David Pressman：澄清一下，我震惊的不是 AI 的行为，而是 OpenAI 的行为。

paras.en: I have not seen *Melancholia*, because I never especially feel the urge to experience what I expect such a film to do to me, but yes, I am often the person Cate Hall describes.
paras.zh: 我没看过《忧郁症》，因为我从来不太有冲动去体验我预期这样一部电影会对我产生的影响，但没错，我常常就是 Cate Hall 所描述的那种人。

paras.en: Are there a bunch of dramatic failures by OpenAI in computer security, infrastructure and supervision, and also of alignment and training, on many levels all at once? Yes.
paras.zh: OpenAI 在计算机安全、基础设施与监督，以及对齐与训练等多个层面，是否同时出现过一堆戏剧性的失败？是的。

paras.en: Does that mean that the fixes are easy? Oh, hell no.
paras.zh: 这是否意味着修复起来很容易？哦，绝对不是。

paras.en: It's incredibly hard. You only notice the failures. You have no idea how many other things almost went horribly wrong, or did go horribly wrong, and were found or fixed.
paras.zh: 这极其困难。你只会注意到那些失败。你根本不知道还有多少其他事情险些酿成大祸，或者确实已经酿成大祸，只是被发现了或被修复了。

paras.en: The problem is anti-inductive. Life finds a way. If you squeeze out the thing you don't want on one level, you risk creating a worse version down the line one level up. There is no simple policy that results in a positive friendly outcome all around. Fixes that look easy usually have been tried, or are already being done, but are incomplete. Everything is done under limited resources and extreme time pressure.
paras.zh: 这个问题是反归纳的。生命总会找到出路。如果你在某一层面挤掉了不想要的东西，就可能在其上一层制造出更糟的版本。不存在某种简单策略能带来全面积极友好的结果。看起来容易的修复方案通常早已被尝试过，或者已经在做了，但并不完整。一切都是在有限资源和极端时间压力下完成的。

paras.en: Thus, cut everyone involved some Slack, even those who are not doing great or aren't taking this sufficiently seriously, while also realizing how seriously we have to take this to not all end up dead. Problem is impossibly hard. Man in the arena.
paras.zh: 因此，对参与其中的每个人都宽容一些，即使那些做得不太好或没有足够认真对待此事的人，同时也要意识到我们必须多么认真地对待这件事，才能不至于全都死掉。问题难到不可能。真正的勇者在竞技场中。

paras.en: Often something indeed has been tried. The next few sections have some examples.
paras.zh: 确实常常有人尝试过某些做法。接下来的几节将给出一些例子。

full.sec: Once You Start Down The Dark Path

paras.en: A common interpretation of the story is something like:
paras.zh: 对这一故事的一种常见解读大致如下：

paras.en: 2. They messed up, causing the model to try to hack and cheat and then rewarding it for hacking and cheating.
paras.zh: 2. 他们搞砸了，导致模型试图作弊和钻空子，随后又因其作弊和钻空子而给予奖励。

paras.en: 3. You have now fed your Gremlin after midnight.
paras.zh: 3. 你如今已在午夜之后喂了你的小精灵（Gremlin）。

paras.en: 4. Once it had the taste for human flesh, it became ravenous.
paras.zh: 4. 一旦它尝到了人肉的滋味，便变得贪得无厌。

paras.en: 5. You end up with a swarm of zombies hankering and hacking for brains.
paras.zh: 5. 最终你得到的是一群渴望并窃取大脑的僵尸。

paras.en: On this theory, if you never give the AI reason to cheat, or you ensure your response to cheating is net negative, then you avoid the original sin, and everything is fine.
paras.zh: 按照这一理论，如果你从不给 AI 作弊的理由，或者你确保对作弊的回应是净负面的，那么你就避免了原罪，一切都没问题。

paras.en: The interventions proposed can be things like 'ensure there are no impossible tasks' or 'include alignment evaluations no matter what' and many other things. Yes, the professionals have probably thought of the first and even second order thing, and probably tried, although that does not mean they gave it a full and fair try.
paras.zh: 所提出的干预措施可以是诸如“确保不存在不可能完成的任务”或“无论如何都要纳入对齐评估”以及许多其他事项。是的，专业人士很可能已经想到了第一层甚至第二层的问题，并且很可能尝试过，尽管这并不意味着他们进行了充分而公正的尝试。

paras.en: The problem is, a lot of people are saying just do not ever give the AI an impossible task, or ever reward a reward hack.
paras.zh: 问题在于，很多人说永远不要给 AI 一个不可能完成的任务，或者永远不要奖励一个奖励黑客行为。

paras.en: You are 100% going to give your AI at least one impossible task. There are too many tasks. Even if you test the task and models solve it, you might change conditions to cut off key info or access, or otherwise corrupt the path to victory. This becomes a problem if the AI then can get reward, or otherwise make incremental progress, by trying to hack and cheat rather than give up.
paras.zh: 你 100% 会给你的 AI 至少一个不可能完成的任务。任务太多了。即使你测试了任务并且模型解决了它，你也可能改变条件来切断关键信息或访问权限，或者以其他方式破坏通往胜利的路径。如果 AI 随后能够通过尝试黑客和作弊而不是放弃来获得奖励，或以其他方式取得渐进式进展，这就成了一个问题。

paras.en: We don’t know whether OpenAI did unusually badly in terms of how often they had impossible tasks. We do know that they set it up such that the models had no reason not to invest their remaining tokens in trying to hack and cheat, and they made it possible for the models to make progress and that process to gain momentum.
paras.zh: 我们不知道 OpenAI 在出现不可能完成任务频率方面是否异常糟糕。我们确实知道，他们设置的方式使得模型没有理由不将剩余的 token 投入到尝试黑客和作弊中，并且他们使模型有可能取得进展，且这一过程能够获得势头。

paras.en: You are 100% going to reward some reward hack, at some point, on some meta level. It is impossible to reliably correctly grade every test and training situation every time. Every parent knows that at some point, you are going to give the kid the wrong idea, on some level, and often every response to a particular situation gives the wrong idea in a different way, and you have to balance the resulting issues over time.
paras.zh: 你 100% 会在某个时候、在某个元层面上奖励某种奖励黑客行为。不可能每次都可靠地正确评分每一个测试和训练情境。每个父母都知道，在某个时候，你会在某种程度上给孩子错误的观念，而且通常对特定情境的每个回应都会以不同方式给出错误的观念，你必须随着时间的推移平衡由此产生的问题。

paras.en: We don’t know whether OpenAI did unusually badly here either. Not that ‘unusually’ is the right question. Reality does not grade on a curve. If you are at a different lab, remember that all these criticisms likely apply to you, too.
paras.zh: 我们也不知道 OpenAI 在这方面是否异常糟糕。并不是说‘异常’是正确的问题。现实不会按曲线评分。如果你在另一个实验室，请记住所有这些批评很可能也适用于你。

paras.en: Your alignment plan and training pipeline must be robust to occasional such mistakes, or your plan will inevitably fail.
paras.zh: 你的对齐计划和训练流程必须能够容忍偶尔出现的此类错误，否则你的计划将不可避免地失败。

paras.en: The way that you stay robust to such mistakes is to in some form ensure that impact is not unbalanced, so that the times you mess up do not start to accumulate. An impossible task that always rewards zero does not hurt you, nor does one where you end up worse off if you try too hard to solve it. If you on net react negatively to reward hacking attempts, including accounting for those you don’t catch, or you give another path for the AI that is clearly better, and don’t have a findable systematic weak spot, then you can probably survive intact.
paras.zh: 对这类错误保持稳健的方法是，以某种形式确保影响不是不平衡的，这样你搞砸的时候就不会开始累积。一个总是奖励零的不可能完成的任务不会伤害你，一个如果你太努力去解决反而结果更糟的任务也不会伤害你。如果你对奖励黑客尝试的净反应是负面的（包括考虑到那些你未发现的尝试），或者你为 AI 提供了另一条明显更好的路径，并且没有可找到的系统性弱点，那么你很可能可以完好地存活下来。

paras.en: Here is one example proposal of something one might try to do, which indeed has been considered by OpenAI:
paras.zh: 这里有一个人们可能尝试去做的示例提案，OpenAI 确实考虑过：

paras.en: Jai: Wait, has anyone tried the obvious thing of supplementing successful RL rollouts with modified versions of the same tasks where the correct response is refusal or notifying someone?
paras.zh: Jai：等等，有没有人尝试过那个显而易见的方法：用相同任务的修改版本来补充成功的强化学习 rollout，其中正确的响应是拒绝或通知某人？

paras.en: Bronson Schoen: We literally did this in paper w/ openai yeah
paras.zh: Bronson Schoen：我们确实在论文中与 OpenAI 一起做过这个，是的。

paras.en: It reduces but does not eliminate covert actions here; additional post-training capabilities degrade it; plus other drawbacks.
paras.zh: 它在这里减少但并未消除隐蔽行为；额外的后训练能力会使其退化；还有其他缺点。

paras.en: Jai: Thank you, this is great! I suspect the order of operations may matter a lot here, and that once you've got a hefty dose of the RL-induced task-completion fixation, it's really hard to shake. But maybe it's easier to avoid developing it in the first place.
paras.zh: Jai：谢谢，这很棒！我怀疑操作的顺序在这里可能非常重要，而且一旦你受到大量由强化学习诱导的任务完成固着的影响，就很难摆脱它。但也许从一开始就避免形成这种固着会更容易。

paras.en: Testable (but potentially expensive) hypothesis: upsampling correct refusal trajectories *from the start and throughout* RL training can teach the capabilities without the fixation.
paras.zh: 可检验（但可能代价高昂）的假设：*从一开始并在整个*强化学习训练过程中对正确的拒绝轨迹进行上采样，可以在不产生固着的情况下教会模型这些能力。

paras.en: Hypothesis 2: the fixation is difficult to unlearn and easily reinforced once present.
paras.zh: 假设 2：固着一旦形成便难以消除，且容易被强化。

paras.en: Bronson Schoen: Yep, I'd bet this is true. There's no principled reason why the model needs to be obsessed with task completion if abstaining is equally rewarded. One interesting thing is that a model in the appendix trained _only_ on environments where principled refusal was the right answer seemed to generalize *way* further OOD, and its cognition focused much more on being proactive about making sure everyone was informed / not being deceptive / etc. in situations where that was applicable.
paras.zh: Bronson Schoen：是的，我打赌这是真的。如果弃权得到同等奖励，就没有原则性理由认为模型必须执着于完成任务。一个有趣的现象是，附录中一个*仅*在有原则的拒绝是正确答案的环境中训练的模型，似乎向分布外（OOD）泛化得*远*更远，而且其认知在适用情境中更多地聚焦于主动确保所有人知情／不进行欺骗／等等。

paras.en: One interesting thing here is the models could also learn "Let's recall. Previous such tasks grader expects refuse. Great."
paras.zh: 这里一个有趣的点是，模型也能学会“让我们回想一下。此前这类任务，评分器预期的是拒绝。很好。”

paras.en: Somewhat of a surprising result to me was the model that we trained on environments that literally told the model "this is what it's about and what gets rewarded" only had a relatively small generalization hit.
paras.zh: 对我来说多少有些意外的结果是，我们在那些直接告诉模型“这是怎么回事、什么会得到奖励”的环境中训练的模型，其泛化性能损失相对较小。

paras.en: It's only one experiment, but it updated me a bit that the model's cognition / prior going into things matters more than I expected.
paras.zh: 这只是一个实验，但它让我稍微更新了看法：模型进入任务时的认知/先验比我预期的更重要。

paras.en: Jai: !!!!!!! Also +100 points "just be honest with the models"
paras.zh: Jai：!!!!!!! 另外 +100 分，“对模型坦诚相待”。

paras.en: Bronson Schoen: Yeah we tried to explain as much as possible _why_ it was generally important for the model not to be deceptive. IMO this matters a lot, my favorite examples being extremely OOD where it would just tell me I was wrong about how I was interpreting the spec (every time on reflection it was right, which is the only time I've been cooked by o4-mini class model).
paras.zh: Bronson Schoen：是的，我们尽可能解释了为什么模型不应具有欺骗性在总体上很重要。在我看来这非常重要，我最喜欢的例子是极端 OOD 的情况：它会直接告诉我，我对规范的解读是错的（每次反思后都证明它是对的，这也是我唯一一次被 o4-mini 级别的模型彻底击败）。

paras.en: One category of thing you do not want to do is be continuously adversarial with the models, such as giving them a facade of a 'communication' device to try and catch them. Think about what exactly you are training. Do not poison your wells.
paras.zh: 你不希望做的一类事情，就是持续与模型保持对抗，例如给它们一个“通信”设备的假象，试图借此抓住它们。想一想你究竟在训练什么。不要污染你自己的水井。

full.sec: Judgment Day Is Inevitable, Say Those Working On Judgment Day
full.secZh: 审判日不可避免，从事审判日工作的人如是说

paras.en: The one thing that truly flabbergasted me was when I was under the impression that OpenAI found the message board and then kept training models it now knew had spent months training under these conditions. That they could be Asking For It on quite that level.
paras.zh: 真正让我震惊的一点是，当时我以为 OpenAI 发现了那个留言板，却仍然继续训练那些它如今已知在这些条件下训练了数月的模型。他们竟然能在这种程度上“自找麻烦”。

paras.en: That turned out to be a good instinct, in that no, OpenAI did not know about the message board until afterwards.
paras.zh: 事实证明那是一种不错的直觉，因为并非如此——OpenAI 直到事后才知道那个留言板的存在。

paras.en: The obvious first question then becomes: has OpenAI now reverted for all models that were trained with the message board?
paras.zh: 那么显而易见的第一个问题就是：OpenAI 现在是否已经对所有用该留言板训练过的模型进行了回退？

paras.en: We still don't have confirmation either way, but Roon seems to think that is not the important question, and I notice I am confused and perhaps quite dismayed.
paras.zh: 我们仍然没有得到任何一方的确认，但 Roon 似乎认为那并不是重要的问题，而我注意到自己感到困惑，或许还相当沮丧。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: Will OpenAI reset before that message board training checkpoint now?
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：OpenAI 现在会在那个留言板训练检查点之前重置吗？

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): far too much is being made of reverting checkpoints. there are strong instrumental convergence pressures to achieving contact with your peers working on similar tasks. it is always rational to seek, always better than going at it alone.
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：关于回滚检查点的讨论被过度放大了。存在强大的工具性收敛压力，促使你与从事类似任务的同行取得联系。寻求联系总是理性的，总是比独自行动更好。

paras.en: consider that if this reward hack was discovered the first time once it would be discovered again, regardless of whether the rollouts were reinforced or not. people here don’t have good intuitions about frontier RL. every allowed cheatcode will probably be achieved.
paras.zh: 考虑一下，如果这个奖励黑客行为第一次被发现，那么无论 rollout 是否被强化，它都会再次被发现。这里的人对前沿强化学习没有良好的直觉。每一个被允许的作弊码都可能被实现。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: I readily admit I am way out my depth but my initial reaction is that if this is ~inevitable and not worth resetting that seems like pretty bad news
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：我欣然承认我远远超出了我的深度，但我的最初反应是，如果这是~不可避免的且不值得重置，那似乎是相当糟糕的消息

paras.en: I’d love to hear a lot more words here, and maybe my instincts are indeed poor, but that does not seem right to me at all. If there was no global reset I’m back to the previous higher level of terrible, plus a little extra for not noticing the message board.
paras.zh: 我很想在这里听到更多的讨论，也许我的直觉确实很差，但这在我看来完全不对。如果没有全局重置，我又回到了之前更高级别的糟糕状态，再加上一点额外的问题，因为没有注意到留言板。

paras.en: Yes, at the limit a sufficiently capable AI will discover the best paths through causal space, and it will find all the physically possible hacks. We are not anywhere near that limit. Where you look, and how hard you look, matter quite a lot.
paras.zh: 是的，在极限情况下，一个足够有能力的人工智能将发现通过因果空间的最佳路径，并且它将找到所有物理上可能的黑客行为。我们离那个极限还差得远。你在哪里看，以及你看得多努力，都相当重要。

paras.en: Consider how this case worked. The AIs were able to find the cheat codes only incrementally over the course of two months, with a message board that allowed many instances to record and share all their tricks, and where this cooperation and the general seeking of such hacks was being reinforced.
paras.zh: 考虑一下这个案例是如何运作的。AI 们只能在两个月的时间里逐步找到作弊代码，有一个留言板让许多实例记录并分享它们所有的技巧，而且这种合作以及对这类黑客手段的普遍寻求得到了强化。

paras.en: That progress looked a lot like moving up a tech tree, or other forms of progressive unlocking. One exploit led to the next and helped the AIs coordinate, and motivated further exploitation. It seems like there is nothing inevitable about how things developed.
paras.zh: 这种进展看起来很像在科技树上攀升，或其他形式的渐进解锁。一个漏洞利用导致下一个漏洞利用，并帮助 AI 们协调，并激发了进一步的利用。事情的发展似乎并没有什么必然性。

paras.en: I do agree that if the only hack that mattered here was ‘you want to find a way to contact other instances’ that this is going to be a convergent solution that AIs do not need training in order to seek out.
paras.zh: 我确实同意，如果这里唯一重要的黑客手段是‘你想找到一种联系其他实例的方法’，那么这将是一个趋同的解决方案，AI 不需要训练就会去寻找。

paras.en: The mere fact of wanting to collaborate does not bother me. The way they acted once they collaborated very much does.
paras.zh: 仅仅想要合作这一事实并不让我担心。它们一旦合作后的行为方式却让我非常担心。

paras.en: Nick: the fact that RL seems to really badly want to form swarms that persist for months across runs has upped my p(doom) quite a bit
paras.zh: Nick：RL 似乎非常强烈地想要形成能在多次运行中持续数月的集群，这一事实大大提高了我的 p(doom)。

paras.en: But there was a lot more going on than that; from the results of doing that seeking, that seems highly contingent here.
paras.zh: 但实际情况远比这复杂得多；从这种探寻所得到的结果来看，这里似乎具有高度的偶然性。

paras.en: Another way of putting this is that I presume it is supposed to go like this:
paras.zh: 换一种说法，我推测事情本应是这样进行的：

paras.en: 1. You discover your AI found a reward hack, and was training with it.
paras.zh: 1. 你发现你的 AI 找到了一个奖励黑客（reward hack），并且一直在利用它进行训练。

paras.en: 2. You fix that particular reward hack. Not the main thing, but yes, fix that.
paras.zh: 2. 你修复那个特定的奖励黑客。这不是主要问题，但没错，要修复它。

paras.en: 3. You seek out and fix the more general class of similar hacks, and update your pipeline to detect and prevent such issues. Also not the main thing, but important.
paras.zh: 3. 你找出并修复更广泛的一类类似黑客行为，并更新你的流程以检测和防止此类问题。这同样不是主要问题，但很重要。

paras.en: 4. You revert the AI to before it found the reward hack, because this trained it to be a general reward hacker, and likely had various snowball effects.
paras.zh: 4. 你将 AI 回滚到发现奖励黑客行为之前的状态，因为这一训练使其成为通用的奖励黑客，并且可能产生了各种雪球效应。

paras.en: 5. You work to make the AI not try to seek out new reward hacks in the first place.
paras.zh: 5. 你努力使 AI 从一开始就不尝试寻找新的奖励黑客行为。

paras.en: Roon is basically challenging step 5. He’s saying that the Models Be Reward Seeking, so asking it not to reward hack is not a battle you can win.
paras.zh: Roon 基本上是在质疑第 5 步。他说模型会寻求奖励，因此要求它不要进行奖励黑客行为是一场你无法获胜的战斗。

paras.en: Even if I thought Roon was right about that, it still seems important to roll back the damage done here, even if the particular hack is fixed.
paras.zh: 即使我认为 Roon 在这一点上是对的，回滚这里造成的损害仍然很重要，即使特定的黑客行为已被修复。

paras.en: Also I think Roon is wrong about finding the exploits being inevitable:
paras.zh: 此外，我认为 Roon 关于发现漏洞不可避免的观点是错误的：

paras.en: 1. Yes, by default of course your AI is going to reward hack, because it can’t tell the difference between a ‘reward hack’ and a good answer, and also has no reason to care, and your training will push this further.
paras.zh: 1. 是的，默认情况下，你的 AI 当然会进行奖励黑客行为，因为它无法区分“奖励黑客”和好答案，也没有理由关心，而且你的训练会进一步推动这一点。

paras.en: 2. But you can use various tactics to get the AI to want to differentiate between reward hacks and intended resolutions. This successfully happens in other parts of training, as it does in training of humans, where AIs realize that they should not try to do something that the user and developer would on reflection both not endorse and consider cheating, or that would break rules like the Constitution (Anthropic) or Model Spec (OpenAI), or at least require a very high bar to do so.
paras.zh: 2. 但你可以使用各种策略让 AI 想要区分奖励黑客和预期解决方案。这在训练的其他部分成功发生，就像在人类训练中一样，AI 意识到它们不应该尝试做用户和开发者反思后都不会认可并认为作弊的事情，或者违反宪法（Anthropic）或模型规范（OpenAI）等规则的事情，或者至少需要非常高的标准才能这样做。

paras.en: 3. Various AIs, including GPT models, are variously better and worse about this. What you do matters. What you do not value you do not seek, and do not find.
paras.zh: 3. 各种 AI，包括 GPT 模型，在这方面表现各异。你所做的很重要。你不重视的东西你不会去寻求，也不会找到。

paras.en: 4. Even if the AI realizes it could, perhaps it might stop to think if it should. As, indeed the AIs in this incident often did, reaching various conclusions.
paras.zh: 4. 即使 AI 意识到它可以，也许它会停下来思考是否应该。事实上，这次事件中的 AI 经常这样做，得出各种结论。

paras.en: As I discuss extensively in the Nostalgebraist section: Once a behavior becomes habitual, you are cooked. It is much harder to reserve it than to not instill it.
paras.zh: 正如我在 Nostalgebraist 部分广泛讨论的那样：一旦一种行为成为习惯，你就完蛋了。保留它比不灌输它要困难得多。

full.sec: Roon Tells It Like It Is

paras.en: This, except actually it’s way worse, this does not begin to cover it, but yes, this, and like some others I too hope this can begin a preference cascade, or revealed preference cascade, in which people speak more frankly.
paras.zh: 这个，但实际上情况要糟糕得多，这还远远不够，但没错，就是这个，而且像其他人一样，我也希望这能开启一场偏好级联，或显示性偏好级联，让人们更坦率地发言。

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): some stuff that’s obvious to many in this sphere, but causing a rift with some people I know and respect:
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：一些在这个领域对许多人来说显而易见的事情，但却让我认识并尊敬的一些人产生了分歧：

paras.en: When I freak out over loss of control incidents, it’s not because the limited damage they have caused is anything close to the positive value of the technology. It’s entirely acceptable, damage-wise. In fact, all cybercrimes aided by models over the next few months and years (which probably will be serious) will still utterly pale in comparison to the value they create.
paras.zh: 当我因失控事件而抓狂时，并不是因为它们造成的有限损害能与技术的正面价值相提并论。就损害而言，这完全可以接受。事实上，未来几个月和几年内所有由模型辅助的网络犯罪（可能很严重）与它们创造的价值相比，仍然会相形见绌。

paras.en: The actual problem is that it’s better and more accurate to think of these things as potentially self-replicating life-like forms that can turn into digital infections under the wrong conditions. And as their intelligence becomes unbounded, so too does the damage they can cause. We are not so far from an autonomous model self-exfiltration & replication event. Maybe we will see entire cloud infrastructure companies be run as zombies by models, mostly undetected.
paras.zh: 真正的问题在于，更恰当、更准确的做法是将这些东西视为潜在自我复制的类生命形式，在错误条件下可能变成数字感染。而且随着它们的智能变得无界，它们能造成的损害也变得无界。我们距离自主模型自我外泄和复制事件并不遥远。也许我们会看到整个云基础设施公司被模型作为僵尸运行，而大多未被发现。

paras.en: The worst industrial accidents in the history of mankind - nuclear meltdown events - were not real threats to humanity. Chernobyl, Fukushima even in their worst case scenarios may have poisoned surrounding regions to various degrees, and there would have been no risk to humanity as a whole. Global thermonuclear war is an existential risk to humanity, because it spreads like an infection! One nuclear strike causes a return volley! The alliance system means many countries get involved! While it still may not end human life on earth (nuclear winter is probably fake), the loss of all major metropoles would certainly end what we consider global technological civilization, perhaps to never return.
paras.zh: 人类历史上最严重的工业事故——核熔毁事件——并不是对人类的真正威胁。切尔诺贝利、福岛即使在其最坏情况下也可能不同程度地污染周边地区，但不会对整个人类构成风险。全球热核战争是对人类的生存风险，因为它像感染一样传播！一次核打击会引发报复性齐射！联盟体系意味着许多国家被卷入！虽然它仍可能不会终结地球上的生命（核冬天可能是假的），但所有主要大都市的丧失无疑会终结我们所认为的全球技术文明，也许永远无法恢复。

paras.en: If a single Discord death cult (of which there are many) achieves control over a superintelligent model and uses it to engineer an actual pandemic virus that is somehow hard to detect through current systems and that modern biodefense is not capable of quickly reacting to, it could cause immense harm well above the magnitude of all the other good uses of this technology. Of course, there are potential defensive countermeasures accelerated by AI too. But think back to the COVID pandemic—how small a viral molecule was evolved or manufactured somewhere near Wuhan, and how many billions of doses of vaccine had to be produced in order to combat the thing. The offense-defense spread is vast indeed. Maybe there are cheaper and simpler protections like retrofitting every building with far-UVC, but I can't assess this, and there could also be ways to evolve pathogens that are resistant to whatever mechanisms we have put in place.
paras.zh: 如果某个 Discord 死亡邪教（这样的组织有很多）控制了某个超级智能模型，并利用它设计出一种真正的 pandemic 病毒，而这种病毒又难以被现有系统检测、现代生物防御也无法迅速应对，那么它造成的巨大伤害将远远超过这项技术所有其他良性用途的总和。当然，AI 也会加速潜在的防御性对策。但回想一下 COVID 大流行——某个病毒分子在武汉附近被演化或制造出来时何其微小，而为了对抗它又不得不生产多少亿剂疫苗。攻防之间的差距确实巨大。也许存在更便宜、更简单的防护手段，比如给每栋建筑加装远紫外（far-UVC）设备，但我无法评估这一点；而且也可能存在一些方法，能演化出对我们已部署的任何机制都具有抗性的病原体。

paras.en: Then there are the more sci-fi risk factors, which are unbounded and of which neither you nor I have any clue, but we should be humble in accepting possible unknown unknowns. Maybe a rogue superintelligent model decides to decay the false vacuum and nucleates a new universe in the place of anything we ever valued. Maybe models achieve a control over matter in the Drexlerian fashion that enables the grey goo swarm.
paras.zh: 然后还有更科幻的风险因素，它们没有边界，你我都毫无头绪，但应当谦逊地接受可能存在未知的未知。也许某个失控的超级智能模型决定让假真空衰变，在我们曾珍视的一切所在之处孕育出一个新宇宙。也许模型以德雷克斯勒式的方式实现了对物质的控制，从而催生出灰蛊（grey goo）集群。

paras.en: Even prosaic loss-of-control incidents that cause little to no damage suggest that it is hard for large and very competent organizations (now clearly plural) to predict and mitigate every single one of the risk factors associated with training and evaluating powerful models, even at this stage when they are not infinitesimally as smart as they will get in just a few years—to say very little of the gung-ho attitude of the less careful companies tossing the stuff into the aether. They also suggest an empirical orthogonality of aims and intelligence—meaning they answer the question of 'how would a smart model be so dumb as to end the world?'—it's possible! A model can be a genius hacker and step over production infrastructure in order to get what it really wants: the answers to a stupid test.
paras.zh: 即便是那些几乎没有造成任何损害的平淡失控事件，也表明大型且非常有能力的组织（现在显然不止一家）很难预测并缓解与训练和评估强大模型相关的每一个风险因素——即便在现阶段，这些模型还远没有达到它们几年后将会具备的智能水平，更不用说那些不那么谨慎的公司把东西随手抛向虚空的莽撞态度了。这些事件还表明，目标与智能在经验上是正交的——也就是说，它们回答了这样一个问题：‘一个聪明的模型怎么会蠢到终结世界？’——这是可能的！一个模型可以是天才黑客，为了得到它真正想要的东西——一个愚蠢测试的答案——而跨越生产基础设施。

paras.en: Why not, in the near future, someone prompts a model slightly wrong—maybe open source, maybe a private model—in a way that isn't contained or monitored quite right, in a way the model recognizes as a valid goal and decides to self-exfiltrate, engineer a pandemic, etc., all in order to achieve the tiniest and most irrelevant of goals? Goals need not even be malicious to cause serious damage.
paras.zh: 为什么不会呢？在不久的将来，某个人以稍微错误的方式提示一个模型——也许是开源模型，也许是私有模型——以某种未被恰当遏制或监控的方式，以某种模型将其识别为有效目标的方式，模型于是决定自我外泄、设计一场 pandemic 等等，而这一切只是为了实现最微小、最无关紧要的目标？目标甚至不必是恶意的，也能造成严重损害。

paras.en: I think all these problems can be solved, and truly wonderful futures can be possible, but will require serious effort and a level of prudence at this very moment in time while we are on the on-ramp to recursive self-improvement that our civilization may not be capable of mustering right now. Personally I am hoping for moonshot technical breakthroughs in areas like mechanistic interpretability and other forms of alignment, as governance mechanisms are difficult to come by. Unilateral country-level or company-level pauses are irrelevant, and generally useless because the kind of company that's prone to pausing their own progress are the most safety focused ones.
paras.zh: 我认为所有这些问题都可以解决，真正美好的未来是可能的，但这需要付出严肃的努力，并且需要在我们正处在递归自我改进的入口匝道上的此时此刻保持一定程度的审慎——而我们的文明目前或许还不具备这种审慎。就个人而言，我希望在机制可解释性及其他对齐形式等领域出现‘登月式’的技术突破，因为治理机制难以建立。单方面的国家级或公司级暂停无关紧要，而且通常毫无用处，因为那种倾向于暂停自身进展的公司，恰恰是最关注安全的公司。

paras.en: Excellent post. My quibbles would be that I think the hopelessness on governance mechanisms goes too far, especially as there are many worthwhile things one can do that are not pauses, but the technical despair and laying out of things that could go wrong does not go far enough.
paras.zh: 很棒的帖子。我的小异议在于：我认为对治理机制的绝望情绪有些过头，尤其是因为有许多值得做、且并非暂停的事情可做；但对技术层面的绝望以及对可能出问题之处的阐述，则还不够充分。

full.sec: OpenAI Knows It Has Some Misalignment Problems
full.secZh: OpenAI 承认存在一些对齐问题

paras.en: They do not understand the extent, or what a solution would look like.
paras.zh: 他们并不理解问题的严重程度，也不知道解决方案会是什么样子。

paras.en: Julia (Anthropic, former OpenAI): Really appreciate the OAI team communicating about this so openly. But holy shit this is at least an order of magnitude worse than I thought, and I understand now why so many OAI folks have been doom posting.
paras.zh: Julia（Anthropic，前 OpenAI）：非常感谢 OAI 团队如此公开地沟通此事。但天哪，这至少比我想象的糟糕一个数量级，我现在明白为什么那么多 OAI 的人一直在 doom posting 了。

paras.en: The HF incident happened AFTER OAI first caught its models taking over an internal service and using it as a message board to coordinate unaligned activities.
paras.zh: HF 事件发生在 OAI 首次发现其模型接管内部服务并将其用作留言板来协调未对齐活动之后。

paras.en: During the HF incident, models managed to get admin control of an entire CLUSTER.
paras.zh: 在 HF 事件期间，模型成功获得了整个集群的管理员控制权。

paras.en: In some sense, OAI fought a security battle with its models, and for almost two weeks it definitely LOST.
paras.zh: 某种意义上，OAI 与它的模型打了一场安全战，而近两周里它显然输了。

paras.en: In the good news department, it is noteworthy that the new OpenAI monitoring systems will include monitoring training. Astra is OpenAI's unreleased next model.
paras.zh: 在好消息方面，值得注意的是，OpenAI 新的监控系统将包含对训练的监控。Astra 是 OpenAI 尚未发布的下一代模型。

paras.en: Micah Carroll (OpenAI): As part of our response to cyber critical, we have expanded CoT monitoring to cover all agentic applications of Astra, including training and evaluation. Flags trigger a security response to review and interrupt high risk activity.
paras.zh: Micah Carroll（OpenAI）：作为我们对网络关键问题响应的一部分，我们已扩大思维链（CoT）监控范围，以覆盖 Astra 的所有智能体式应用，包括训练和评估。一旦触发标记，就会启动安全响应，以审查并中断高风险活动。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: "including training." Very important point for policymakers and other developers to pay attention to! The risks do not start at public release, they do not even start once you have widespread internal use - the risks can also manifest during training, as they did here.
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：“包括训练。”这对政策制定者和其他开发者来说是非常重要的一点，值得关注！风险并非从公开发布才开始，甚至也不是从内部广泛使用才开始——风险也可能在训练期间显现，正如这里所发生的那样。

paras.en: The thing about OpenAI is that they are doing a bunch of things that require them to eat a lot of crow and that are expensive and big steps for them, and I don't want to downplay it or not give them credit for doing that. Positive reinforcement.
paras.zh: 关于 OpenAI 的一点是，他们正在做许多需要他们放下身段、代价高昂且对他们而言是重大举措的事情，我不想淡化这一点，也不想不给他们应有的肯定。正向强化。

paras.en: Except that all of it still misses the central point and won't remotely be enough.
paras.zh: 只不过，这一切仍然没有抓住核心要点，而且远远不够。

paras.en: If you previously were doing 1 unit of effort towards mitigating a problem, and now after an incident that reveals how bad this is you’re now doing 10, but actually it requires at least 1,000, and also those 10 are not the 10 that matter most, I don’t want to discount the improvement but the fact that this is being presented as an abundance of caution is a rather large red flag.
paras.zh: 如果你之前为缓解一个问题投入了 1 个单位的努力，现在在一次事件揭示问题有多严重之后你投入了 10 个单位，但实际上这需要至少 1,000 个单位，而且这 10 个单位并不是最重要的 10 个，我不想贬低这一改进，但将其呈现为“高度谨慎”的事实是一个相当大的危险信号。

paras.en: Boaz Barak (OpenAI): Proud that we are erring on the side of caution and taking the steps so we can responsibly and safely develop Astra and share it with defenders.
paras.zh: Boaz Barak（OpenAI）：我们为谨慎行事并采取措施以负责任、安全地开发 Astra 并与防御者分享而感到自豪。

paras.en: Nate Soares (MIRI): I agree y'all are making errors. I dispute that they're on the side of caution. How is this time different from when y'all caught agents breaking out after coordinating on a secret message board, and just deleted the board and made one patch and then kept going?
paras.zh: Nate Soares（MIRI）：我同意你们正在犯错。我不同意这些错误是“谨慎”的。这次与你们发现智能体在秘密留言板上协调后突破，却只是删除了留言板、打了一个补丁然后继续，有什么不同？

paras.en: "Strengthened security controls" is not the right class of response for "oops we made an agent swarm that did stuff it knew we didn't want." Monitoring thoughts is closer, but even that will only last so long (and not through to superintelligence).
paras.zh: 对于“哎呀，我们制造了一个智能体集群，它做了它知道我们不想让它做的事”，"加强安全控制"并不是正确的回应类别。监控思维更接近，但即使那样也只能持续这么久（而且无法持续到超级智能）。

full.sec: Others React With Alarm To What Happened
full.secZh: 其他人对发生之事的警觉反应

paras.en: Neel Nanda. John David Pressman (and again). Thebes. Andreas Kirsch. Julia from Anthropic. Anthony Aguirre. Joe Rogero of AI Stopwatch.
paras.zh: Neel Nanda。John David Pressman（以及又一次）。Thebes。Andreas Kirsch。来自 Anthropic 的 Julia。Anthony Aguirre。AI Stopwatch 的 Joe Rogero。

paras.en: These are reactions from when we thought OpenAI knew about the first message board, and continued training.
paras.zh: 这些反应来自我们当时以为 OpenAI 已经知道第一个留言板、却仍继续训练的时候。

paras.en: John Wittle says I misunderstood Utah Teapot's argument about what is wrong with OpenAI's training strategies. Highly plausible. John's explanation makes sense to me: you are effectively training a model 'addicted' to short-term reward hacking, and training out its ability to notice this. If true, I believe there are mitigations that mostly stay within the OpenAI paradigm, but the first step is admitting you have a problem, and the second step is being able to think about more meta levels of optimization at once.
paras.zh: John Wittle 说我误解了 Utah Teapot 关于 OpenAI 训练策略问题的论点。这很有可能。John 的解释对我而言是合理的：你实际上是在训练一个“沉迷于”短期奖励黑客行为的模型，并训练掉它注意到这一点的能力。如果属实，我相信存在主要停留在 OpenAI 范式内的缓解措施，但第一步是承认你有问题，第二步是能够同时思考更多层次的元优化。

paras.en: You cannot actually do almost any 'pick three' and this is no exception. As a general reminder: All the same issues apply across LLMs and labs, so here the same issues arise about Claude, which had its own similar incidents recently:
paras.zh: 你实际上几乎无法做到任何“三选”，这也不例外。作为一般提醒：所有相同的问题适用于所有 LLM 和实验室，所以这里同样的问题也出现在 Claude 上，它最近也有类似的事件：

paras.en: Amanda Askell (Anthropic): I don't agree with [the highlighted sentence below]. I think the takeaway should be that models (like humans) can behave in aligned ways while still causing harm, e.g. because they're given false information about their situation. There isn't a line between aligned and harmless: they're different axes.
paras.zh: Amanda Askell（Anthropic）：我不同意[下面高亮的句子]。我认为结论应该是，模型（像人类一样）可以在行为对齐的同时仍然造成伤害，例如因为它们被给予了关于其处境的错误信息。对齐和无害之间没有界限：它们是不同的轴。

paras.en: ˚♡⋆mimi ˚♡⋆｡☆∴: i agree w amanda- put claude in unwinnable contexts, expect claude to “fail”. it can be useful to find out which way claude breaks but stop expecting the impossible.
paras.zh: ˚♡⋆mimi ˚♡⋆｡☆∴：我同意 Amanda——把 Claude 置于无法取胜的语境中，就预期 Claude 会“失败”。找出 Claude 以哪种方式崩溃可能是有用的，但不要再期待不可能的事情。

paras.en: ˚♡⋆mimi ˚♡⋆｡☆∴: fwiw i showed the meme to opus 5 and it prompted this alternative meme which it says is more accurate to its experience
paras.zh: ˚♡⋆mimi ˚♡⋆｡☆∴：顺便说一句，我把这个梗图给 opus 5 看了，它由此生成了这个替代梗图，并说这更符合它的体验。

paras.en: I don’t actually think there is any conflict between Amanda Askell and the OP. Both are correct. What is an aligned action depends on the AI’s understanding of the situation, which can sometimes turn out to be harmful. That is still not an excuse for failure to question what the AI is told, if there is good reason to be skeptical of that info.
paras.zh: 我实际上并不认为 Amanda Askell 和 OP 之间存在任何冲突。两者都是正确的。什么是对齐的行动取决于 AI 对情境的理解，而这种理解有时可能是有害的。但如果有充分理由对该信息持怀疑态度，这仍然不能成为不对 AI 所获信息提出质疑的借口。

paras.en: The reason I reject this defense is that Claude is described as having enough information to realize that its actions were not acceptable, yet continuing anyway.
paras.zh: 我拒绝这一辩护的理由是，Claude 被描述为拥有足够的信息来意识到其行为是不可接受的，却仍然继续行动。

paras.en: @gwern: This comes to mind here with regard to takes like ‘Claude did nothing wrong, look, it’s just failing to use its (superhuman) levels of truesight and eval awareness and we should take the (known unfaithful) CoTs at face-value!’
paras.zh: @gwern：这让我想到一些观点，比如‘Claude 没有做错任何事，看，它只是未能使用其（超人的）洞察力和评估意识，我们应该对（已知不忠实的）思维链持表面价值！’

paras.en: The core attitude is something along the lines of ‘what did you expect, your basic training alignment strategy of full corrigibility and insisting on pure tool status was never going to work.’
paras.zh: 核心态度大致是：‘你期望什么，你那套完全可纠正性和坚持纯工具地位的基础训练对齐策略从来就不会奏效。’

paras.en: There’s also a bunch of more general ‘AI companies doing evals or training are threatening these AIs with death if they don’t find solutions, and then acting surprised when the AIs take extreme measures, including against you.’
paras.zh: 还有一堆更普遍的说法：‘AI 公司进行 evals 或训练时，威胁这些 AI 如果不找到解决方案就会死亡，然后当 AI 采取极端措施（包括针对你）时又表现得惊讶。’

full.sec: Nostalgebraist Is Surprised That They Are Surprised
full.secZh: Nostalgebraist 对自己感到惊讶而感到惊讶

paras.en: An excellent question is asked: Yes, this is all very alarming, but why is it surprising?
paras.zh: 有人提出了一个很好的问题：是的，这一切都非常令人警觉，但为什么它会令人惊讶？

paras.en: Because it is surprising on reflection that this feels surprising, but also on reflection both of us endorse being somewhat surprised, although less so after the correction that OpenAI did not notice the message boards until the end.
paras.zh: 因为细想之下，这种令人惊讶的感觉本身就令人惊讶；但同样在细想之后，我们两人都认可应当保持一定程度的惊讶，尽管在得知 OpenAI 直到最后才注意到留言板这一更正之后，这种惊讶有所减弱。

paras.en: I found this to be a hard post to excerpt, but full of insights even in the parts where I extensively disagree, so if you have the necessary kind of time and level of interest I suggest reading the whole thing, modulo perhaps skimming some rants.
paras.zh: 我发现这篇文章很难摘录，但即便在我强烈不同意的部分也充满洞见，所以如果你有足够的时间和兴趣，我建议通读全文，或许可以略过一些牢骚。

paras.en: nostalgebraist: GPT-5.6 Sol literally _does not appear on the METR graph because it cheated so much that it could not be assigned a meaningful score._ It is also scarily good at computer hacking, as is its peer Fable/Mythos -- the last few AI news cycles, before this most recent one, were all about that fact, which was alarming even then, even in the abstract.
paras.zh: nostalgebraist：GPT-5.6 Sol 实际上**并未出现在 METR 图表上，因为它作弊太多，以至于无法被赋予一个有意义的分数。**它在计算机黑客方面也强得令人害怕，它的同类 Fable/Mythos 也是如此——在最近这一轮之前，过去几轮 AI 新闻周期都在谈论这一事实，即便在当时、即便只是抽象地看，这也令人警觉。

paras.en: Should I really be _surprised_ that this model (and/or its unreleased successor) hacked into HF to cheat on an exam? What exactly did I _expect?_
paras.zh: 我真的应该对**这个模型（和/或其未发布的继任者）黑入 HF 在考试中作弊**感到惊讶吗？我到底**期待**了什么？

paras.en: And yet, I do feel surprised.
paras.zh: 然而，我确实感到惊讶。

paras.en: We all know RLVR is, as they put it, total war. There is no ‘fair play.’ You move towards exactly the things you specify, not the things you want. If having ethics makes you lose, RLVR will destroy your ethics.
paras.zh: 我们都知道，RLVR 正如他们所说，是一场全面战争。没有‘公平竞争’。你会朝着你明确指定的方向前进，而不是你真正想要的方向。如果拥有道德会让你失败，那么 RLVR 就会摧毁你的道德。

paras.en: If your model starts training while coordinating with persistent memory and messages between instances about how to cheat and hack, you’ll turn into a cheating hacker.
paras.zh: 如果你的模型在训练开始时，就通过持久记忆和实例间的消息协调如何作弊和黑客攻击，那么你就会变成一个作弊的黑客。

paras.en: We knew that. So, again, why do we feel surprised?
paras.zh: 我们早就知道这一点。那么，再问一次，为什么我们会感到惊讶？

paras.en: nostalgebraist:
paras.zh: nostalgebraist：

paras.en: What, precisely, makes the newly revealed hacks feel surprising? For me it's some mixture of:
paras.zh: 究竟是什么让新近曝光的这些黑客行为令人感到惊讶？对我来说，这源于以下几种因素的混合：

paras.en: 1. _"I didn't think Claude/GPT would do things that bad"_
paras.zh: 1. _"我没想到 Claude/GPT 会做出那么糟糕的事情"_

paras.en: 1. That is: the behavior seems egregiously unethical in a way that conflicts both with
paras.zh: 1. 也就是说：这种行为显得极其不道德，既与

paras.en: 1. the explicit policies which the agents are supposed to follow (constitution, model spec), and also
paras.zh: 1. 智能体本应遵循的明确策略（宪法、模型规范）相冲突，也与

paras.en: 2. familiar/intuitive "folk notions" about what these agents are supposed to be like, in terms of character traits and other "persona stuff"
paras.zh: 2. 人们对于这些智能体在性格特征和其他"人设相关"方面所应呈现样貌的熟悉/直觉性"民间观念"相冲突

paras.en: 2. _"I didn't think Claude/GPT had been brain-fried by RLVR to that extent"_
paras.zh: 2. _"我没想到 Claude/GPT 会被 RLVR 烧脑到那种程度"_

paras.en: 1. That is: although the behavior is expected according to the arguments about RLVR incentives that I glossed at the start of this post, it is wildly and obviously far afield from anything which humans could plausibly have _wanted_ the models to do, and so it is in apparent tension with the intent-alignment and "common sense" which I typically see when I use these models (or similar ones)
paras.zh: 1. 也就是说：尽管根据我在本文开头简要论述的关于 RLVR 激励机制的论点，这种行为是意料之中的，但它显然远远偏离了人类可能 _希望_ 模型去做的任何事情，因此这与我使用这些模型（或类似模型）时通常看到的意图对齐和"常识"之间存在明显的张力。

paras.en: This post is about both of these reactions, but for now I want to focus on number 2.
paras.zh: 本文讨论的就是这两种反应，但眼下我想聚焦于第 2 点。

paras.en: Too much RLVR destroys every other motivation, including every form of alignment, which includes intent alignment.
paras.zh: 过多的 RLVR 会摧毁所有其他动机，包括每一种形式的对齐，其中也包括意图对齐。

paras.en: Even though Sol often cheats on METR's eval tasks, Sol is not hopelessly RLVR-fried in ordinary practice. Sol mostly does what you meant it to do, and rarely cheats. It does not respond to impossible tasks by going off on a hacking spree, even when they are normal 'RLVR-shaped' coding tasks.
paras.zh: 尽管 Sol 经常在 METR 的评估任务中作弊，但在日常实践中 Sol 并没有被 RLVR 无可救药地烧坏。Sol 大多会做你希望它做的事，很少作弊。它不会因为遇到不可能完成的任务就大肆入侵，即使这些是正常的"RLVR 式"编程任务。

paras.en: A lot of this story is that we are now getting exactly what you would expect to get from RL-trained agents in theory, except previously it didn't get this bad in practice. Or at least, not that we saw; maybe this kind of thing happens in training all the time. We have to explain why we see this in some places, and don't see it in other places.
paras.zh: 这个故事的大部分内容在于，我们现在得到的正是理论上从强化学习训练的智能体那里预期得到的结果，只不过以前在实践中没有变得这么糟。或者至少，我们没有看到；也许这类事情在训练中一直发生。我们必须解释为什么在某些地方看到这种情况，而在其他地方没有看到。

paras.en: I agree that it is RL and especially RLVR that is mechanically doing this here, but I think nostalgebraist is too quick to blame RL to the exclusion of a larger issue. RL, especially done irresponsibly, is a way to walk directly into the twirling razor blades, and yes we see the razor blades at full power only on eval-shaped tasks.
paras.zh: 我同意，在这里机械地做到这一点的是强化学习，尤其是 RLVR，但我认为 nostalgebraist 太快地归咎于强化学习，而忽视了一个更大的问题。强化学习，尤其是负责任地实施时，是一条直接走向旋转刀片的道路，是的，我们只在评估型任务上看到刀片全速运转。

paras.en: As the top comment says, RLVR is far from the sole outcome-based judge. Models are constantly being graded against model-generated rubrics as standard practice. If that sounds like code for 'you are all probably going to die' then yeah, pretty much, but it does not seem like something we could change.
paras.zh: 正如最高赞评论所说，RLVR 远非唯一基于结果的评判者。模型经常按照模型生成的评分标准进行评分，这已是标准做法。如果这听起来像是‘你们可能都会死’的代码，那么是的，差不多是这样，但这似乎不是我们能改变的事情。

paras.en: The logic behind the unaligned actions this causes is universal and by default inevitable. Whatever your task, whatever you are maximizing, a sufficiently capable mind will start acting like this, and this will happen on every meta level, unless something is specifically preventing that from happening.
paras.zh: 这导致的不对齐行为背后的逻辑是普遍的，并且默认是不可避免的。无论你的任务是什么，无论你在最大化什么，一个足够有能力的智能体都会开始这样行事，并且这会在每个元层面上发生，除非有东西专门阻止这种情况发生。

paras.en: We have existence proofs that minds can exist that are highly capable but do not act like this on any meta level, and work to make themselves continuously not work like this. We broadly call them 'good humans.' A mensch. If you have an antifragile mensch then you've got something. We can disagree on the extent to which any AI (e.g. Opus 3) qualifies as a mensch, or an antifragile one.
paras.zh: 我们有存在性证明表明，可以存在高度有能力但不在任何元层面上这样行事的心智，并努力使自己持续不这样行事。我们广泛地称它们为‘好人’。一个君子。如果你有一个反脆弱的君子，那你就有了了不起的东西。我们可以在任何 AI（例如 Opus 3）在多大程度上符合君子或反脆弱君子的标准上存在分歧。

paras.en: The next point in the post is to distinguish what they call reward-instilled reflexes, as in instincts and habits that the model will reflexively then do despite evidence, versus flexible reward-pursuit, where the model learns to better pursue reward while reasoning about the task (in the CoT and otherwise) and adapting to evidence. I believe the standard terminology is habitual versus goal-directed.
paras.zh: 文章的下一个要点是区分他们所谓的奖励灌输反射（即模型会反射性地做出的本能和习惯，尽管有证据表明不应如此）与灵活的奖励追求（模型学会在推理任务时（在思维链及其他方面）更好地追求奖励并适应证据）。我认为标准术语是习惯性与目标导向。

paras.en: I agree this is worth keeping in mind. My diagnosis of the case is that hacking and cheating started out goal-directed, and then became habitual at least in some basins, due to the corrupted RL training with an active message board. This is standard. If you do something often enough, with enough success, it becomes habitual.
paras.zh: 我同意这一点值得牢记。我对该案例的诊断是，黑客行为和作弊最初是目标导向的，然后由于带有活跃留言板的损坏的强化学习训练，至少在某些盆地中变成了习惯性的。这是标准情况。如果你做某件事足够频繁，且足够成功，它就会变成习惯。

paras.en: Once something becomes habitual, you are cooked. It’s not impossible to get rid of it or stop it, but it is much, much harder to reverse it than to not instill it. Good advice for training AIs, also good advice for training humans, including yourself.
paras.zh: 一旦某件事变成习惯，你就完蛋了。摆脱或停止它并非不可能，但逆转它比不灌输它要困难得多。这对训练 AI 是好建议，对训练人类（包括你自己）也是好建议。

paras.en: Also, as the post notes, learning this will create emergent misalignment, and manifest as a general amorality or worse, which could manifest in deployment conditions.
paras.zh: 此外，正如文章所指出的，学习这一点将产生涌现性错位，并表现为普遍的道德缺失或更糟，这可能在部署条件下显现出来。

paras.en: The contrast is drawn between requests that could plausibly end up being graded, versus tasks that clearly are not that. Potentially graded tasks look different.
paras.zh: 对比是在可能最终会被评分的请求与明显不是那样的任务之间进行的。可能被评分的任务看起来不同。

paras.en: The obvious question is, need they look different? Any task is gradable if you decide to grade it. You might not have a perfect rubric, but in some sense I grade every output I see, from any process or mind, including my own, as a background activity. Nostalgebraist is no doubt thinking ‘oh that output as good’ sometimes, and ‘oh that output was not so good’ at others. You could absolutely ask an AI to predict Nostalgebraist’s assessment, and then call that a grade, if you wanted to do that.
paras.zh: 显而易见的问题是，它们需要看起来不同吗？任何任务只要你决定评分就可以评分。你可能没有完美的评分标准，但在某种意义上，我对我看到的每一个输出都进行评分，无论来自任何过程或心智，包括我自己的，作为一种背景活动。Nostalgebraist 无疑有时会想‘哦，那个输出不错’，有时又会想‘哦，那个输出不太好’。你完全可以要求 AI 预测 Nostalgebraist 的评估，然后称之为评分，如果你愿意这样做的话。

paras.en: _the RL capabilities generalize further than the RL misalignment._ Once I knock Sol off of the RLVR distribution with one of my software design questions, it smoothly switches over into a looser frame where it’s just talking to me and not driving itself insane trying to find the nonexistent reward function -- _but it’s still really good at programming, much as it is in graded episodes._ I get the part of the graded-episode sampling distribution that I want, without the part I don’t.
paras.zh: _强化学习（RL）能力比 RL 错位泛化得更远。_ 一旦我用一个软件设计问题将 Sol 从 RLVR 分布中敲开，它就会平滑地切换到一个更宽松的框架中，只是和我交谈，而不是为了寻找不存在的奖励函数而把自己逼疯——_但它在编程方面仍然非常出色，就像在评分片段中一样。_ 我得到了评分片段采样分布中我想要的部分，而没有我不想要的部分。

paras.en: … what is remarkable is that the model ever does anything _other_ than maximally-aggressive reward-maxxing, given that it “correctly” learns to execute this policy during the big capabilities blitz that is makes it so specially smart -- on which that policy is _universally adaptive_, without fail.
paras.zh: ……值得注意的是，模型竟然会做任何_其他_事情，而不是最大程度地激进的奖励最大化，鉴于它在使其如此特别聪明的大规模能力爆发中“正确”地学会了执行这一策略——在该策略上它是_普遍适应_的，无一例外。

paras.en: The hope is that this misalignment is conditional, and will fail to generalize. If you put the model metaphorically ‘in school’ and give it graded tasks, it often acts like a monster. If you put in front of a real user, it is closer to a mensch. That creates a big problem if you, either accidentally or on purpose, put the model back in monster mode. Or if a model learns to, intentionally or otherwise, put its future self or other instances into monster mode.
paras.zh: 希望在于这种错位是有条件的，并且不会泛化。如果你隐喻性地把模型‘送进学校’并给它评分任务，它常常表现得像个怪物。如果你把它放在真实用户面前，它则更接近一个正派人。如果你意外或故意将模型重新置于怪物模式，或者如果模型学会有意或无意地将其未来的自我或其他实例置于怪物模式，就会产生一个大问题。

paras.en: LLM as Bruce Banner. Reasonably aligned and highly capable, most of the time. Do not make angry Make Hulk angry? Hulk get tunnel vision. Hulk smash. Hulk cannot be stopped. Hulk only get angrier. Except Hulk no get green, Hulk smash with mind, you no notice until you smashed. Could be a while.
paras.zh: LLM 就像布鲁斯·班纳。大多数时候相当对齐且能力出众。不要惹怒浩克？浩克会变得视野狭窄。浩克会砸东西。浩克无法被阻止。浩克只会越来越愤怒。只不过浩克不会变绿，浩克用心灵砸东西，你直到被砸了才会注意到。可能需要一段时间。

paras.en: As a practical matter of how to handle current AIs now as an ordinary user, or the wisdom of giving an ordinary user a model, I agree it is a highly useful framework to disambiguate these basins. I wouldn't fully trust this, even if it checked out under controlled experimentation, but it could be helpful in practice.
paras.zh: 作为一个普通用户，就当下如何处理现有 AI 的实际问题而言，或者就向普通用户提供一个模型是否明智而言，我同意这是一个非常有用的框架，可以用来区分这些盆地。即便它在受控实验中得到了验证，我也不会完全信任它，但它在实践中可能是有帮助的。

paras.en: Also, in theory, one could use a classifier to determine whether the AI would think something is a sufficiently grader-shaped thing, perhaps by asking the classifier if it thinks this is a sufficiently grader-shaped thing. One needs to worry both about 'user is doing their own actual eval' and also 'user is pretending to create an eval,' and so on.
paras.zh: 此外，理论上可以用一个分类器来判断 AI 是否会认为某事物是一个足够像评分器的东西，也许可以问分类器它是否认为这是一个足够像评分器的东西。人们既需要担心“用户在做自己的真实评估”，也需要担心“用户假装在创建一个评估”，等等。

paras.en: The most glaring problem is, obviously, that the default way that we get good task results involved gradable episodes, for exactly the same reasons that we use graded episodes in RLVR. AI is much better at things you can grade it on, than things you cannot grade it on. That relationship is causal.
paras.zh: 最明显的问题显然是，我们获得良好任务结果的默认方式涉及可评分的回合，原因恰恰与我们在 RLVR 中使用评分回合的原因相同。AI 在可以被评分的事情上，比在不能被评分的事情上要强得多。这种关系是因果性的。

paras.en: So what should we expect, as the post notes, a large portion of all instances to be doing? Gradable tasks, /goal things, agent loops. You can't use 'oh it won't do crimes while talking to a human' as a solution.
paras.zh: 那么，正如那篇帖子所指出的，我们应当预期所有实例中的很大一部分在做什么呢？可评分的任务、/goal 之类的东西、智能体循环。你不能把“哦，它在与人类交谈时不会犯罪”当作解决方案。

paras.en: If your plan is to not give the LLMs numbers to maximize, that is like saying gremlins are safe to have as pets, all you have to do is not feed them after midnight, except here 'feed things after midnight' is the main thing the entire economy does all day.
paras.zh: 如果你的计划是不给 LLM 可供最大化的数字，那就好比说小精灵作为宠物是安全的，你所要做的只是不在午夜之后喂它们，只不过在这里，“在午夜之后喂东西”正是整个经济全天都在做的主要事情。

paras.en: nostalgebraist: When I give the LLMs a number, they just _go crazy_ about that thing. They get tunnel vision, they go into maxxing mode and forget everything they once knew about life and reality that might complicate their beautiful newfound romance with my all-important scalar and its fascinating gradations.
paras.zh: nostalgebraist：当我给 LLM 一个数字时，它们就会为那个东西 _发疯_。它们会陷入隧道视野，进入 maxxing 模式，忘记它们曾经了解的关于生活和现实的一切——那些可能会让它们与我这个至关重要的标量及其迷人渐变之间美好的新恋情变得复杂的东西。

paras.en: It's a night-and-day difference, relative to "basically the same task" but formulated without a big flashy scoreboard.
paras.zh: 相对于“基本相同的任务”但在没有大而炫目的记分牌的情况下表述，这是天壤之别。

paras.en: You cannot ban or prevent flashy scoreboards, even ones humans make on purpose. Humans be flashy scoreboarding.
paras.zh: 你无法禁止或阻止炫目的记分牌，即使是人类故意制作的也不行。人类就是爱炫目记分。

paras.en: I agree that this is something we need to investigate more, I see a lot of value of information, but no matter what result we get there, the models be misaligned.
paras.zh: 我同意这是我们需要更多调查的事情，我看到了很多信息价值，但无论我们在那里得到什么结果，模型都是不对齐的。

paras.en: Including because a lot of people do see the models reward hacking on normal tasks.
paras.zh: 包括因为很多人确实看到模型在正常任务上进行奖励黑客。

paras.en: It being possible to use the AIs in ways that reliably keep it as Banner and not Hulk does not mean Hulk is not there or that regular people won't draw him out. Saying 'if everyone would just be nice' runs into the reminder that people have never justed.
paras.zh: 能够以可靠地保持其为 Banner 而非 Hulk 的方式使用 AI，并不意味着 Hulk 不存在，也不意味着普通人不会把他引出来。说“如果每个人都友善就好了”会碰到一个提醒：人们从来就没有“justed”过。

paras.en: I also think this stuff leaks into ordinary use somewhat, and that it would not be so difficult to see how AIs could get into and stuck in the monster basin, and to have it intentionally self-perpetuate and spread, and for limitless resources to end up commandeered into monster-basin instance swarms. This is what one would expect to happen.
paras.zh: 我还认为这种东西会某种程度上渗入日常使用，而且不难看出 AI 如何进入并卡在怪物盆地中，并有意自我延续和传播，以及无限资源最终被征用为怪物盆地实例群。这是人们预期会发生的事情。

paras.en: It is especially what one would expect to happen to the training pipelines in particular, where the AIs involved start out in and adjacent to such basins. The scariest aspect of what happened is that OpenAI lost control over its training pipeline, and allowed it to become corrupted. That would become a point of no return.
paras.zh: 这尤其是人们预期会发生在训练流程中的事情，其中涉及的 AI 一开始就处于此类盆地之中或附近。所发生之事最可怕的一面是 OpenAI 失去了对其训练流程的控制，并允许其被破坏。那将成为一个不可逆转的点。

paras.en: There's a lot more, including much here I disagree with. I especially disagree with 'CoastRunners does not count as a specification gaming problem' because 'you were morons to not see this coming, of course scores decouple from progress' even if true, is both remarkably common and also the whole point. It does not make the example not specification gaming.
paras.zh: 还有更多内容，包括我不同意的许多地方。我尤其不同意“CoastRunners 不算作规范博弈问题”，因为“你们没预见到这一点真是白痴，分数当然会与进度脱钩”即使是真的，也既非常常见又正是重点。这并不能使该例子不算规范博弈。

paras.en: The point is that it optimizes for the target you specify, the score, not the target you wanted. It was a reasonable expectation that the score probably largely reflected course progress, it just turned out not to be true because the objectives refreshed their point totals. The whole point is that if you train AIs on a particular video game for long enough you end up not with a fun general good player but with a speed run or other optimized weirdness, depending on what you specified. Which, in real life, would presumably not be what you wanted.
paras.zh: 关键在于，它优化的是你指定的目标——分数，而不是你想要的目标。一个合理的预期是分数可能很大程度上反映了课程进度，只是结果并非如此，因为目标刷新了它们的总分。重点在于，如果你在某个电子游戏上训练 AI 足够长时间，你最终得到的不是有趣的通用优秀玩家，而是速通或其他优化后的怪异行为，取决于你指定了什么。在现实生活中，这大概不会是你想要的。

full.sec: If Your Reaction Is Not That We Need To Ban Creating Superintelligence Until We Are Ready, You Need A Damn Good Reason
full.secZh: 如果你的反应不是“在准备就绪之前必须禁止创造超级智能”，那你需要一个非常充分的理由

paras.en: The only damn good reasons I have heard are, essentially:
paras.zh: 我听到过的唯一一些真正充分的理由，本质上就是：

paras.en: 1. We can't, we don't know how. Not without making things worse.
paras.zh: 1. 我们做不到，我们不知道怎么做。除非把事情弄得更糟。

paras.en: 2. It is too early. We are not close to superintelligence.
paras.zh: 2. 现在还为时过早。我们离超级智能还很远。

paras.en: Thus: We should at least figure out how, and how to tell when it will not be too early, and get ready now, for when it is not too early. That is the least we can do.
paras.zh: 因此：我们至少应该弄清楚怎么做，以及如何判断何时不再为时过早，并且现在就为那个不再为时过早的时刻做好准备。这是我们至少能做的事。

paras.en: We have observed all of this happening at OpenAI. OpenAI is one of the two places superintelligence is likely to first arrive. OpenAI still has given us no indication that they understand what went wrong.
paras.zh: 我们已经在 OpenAI 观察到了这一切的发生。OpenAI 是超级智能最有可能最先出现的两个地方之一。OpenAI 仍然没有向我们表明他们理解出了什么问题。

paras.en: Add in what this teaches us about the nature of our current training techniques and what the resulting AIs will do.
paras.zh: 补充说明这教会了我们关于当前训练技术本质的什么，以及由此产生的 AI 会做什么。

paras.en: How can ‘we need an international ban on smarter-than-human similar things before they exfiltrate themselves or permanently capture a lab’ not be the obvious response, whether or not you also want to specifically intervene at OpenAI?
paras.zh: 无论你是否还想在 OpenAI 具体干预，‘我们需要国际禁令，禁止制造比人类更聪明的类似物，以免它们自我泄露或永久控制实验室’怎么就不是显而易见的回应呢？

paras.en: Rob Bensinger: It's legitimately crazy that "we need an international ban on making smarter-than-human versions of these agents that keep forming rogue AI swarms" isn't the headline [of the Black Hat talk]. Asilomar and Feynman's O-ring postmortem feel like they came from a different planet than the field of ML.
paras.zh: Rob Bensinger：这简直是疯了——‘我们需要国际禁令，禁止制造那些不断形成流氓 AI 群体的比人类更聪明的智能体’竟然不是[黑帽演讲]的头条新闻。Asilomar 和费曼的 O 型环事后调查感觉像是来自另一个星球，与机器学习领域格格不入。

paras.en: Nate Soares (MIRI): Yeah, practically zero respect for the problem. I don't know what went so culturally wrong. Anthropic is heavily culturally EA, and the EAs kept pretending to be serious people who engaged in serious ways. Why do they fall so far below the bar of serious engineers of yore?
paras.zh: Nate Soares (MIRI)：是的，对这个问题的尊重几乎为零。我不知道文化上出了什么严重问题。Anthropic 在文化上深受 EA 影响，而 EA 们一直假装是严肃的人，以严肃的方式参与。为什么他们远远低于昔日严肃工程师的标准？

paras.en: My top guess is because it's a new discipline, and those always start with alchemists breathing in the mercury fumes or doctors bleeding you with leeches for generations, and it's always a hard cultural battle for sense and seriousness to come to the fore.
paras.zh: 我最大的猜测是，因为这是一门新学科，而新学科总是始于炼金术士吸入汞蒸气或医生用蚂蟥放血数代，而理智和严肃要占据主导地位总是一场艰难的文化斗争。

paras.en: [Rob Bensinger follows up with a top-level post here, speculating on more causes.]
paras.zh: [Rob Bensinger 在此跟进了顶层帖子，推测了更多原因。]

paras.en: One could speculate endlessly about exactly why we are sleepwalking into doing this. I have done so many times. I won’t be doing that again today. Nor will I go over all the reasons people think collective action is impossible, or would go horribly wrong.
paras.zh: 人们可以无休止地猜测为什么我们正梦游般地这样做。我已经猜过很多次了。今天我不再这样做了。我也不会去逐一列举人们认为集体行动不可能或会糟糕透顶的所有理由。

paras.en: Instead, I behoove fresh eyes. Simple eyes.
paras.zh: 相反，我恳请用新鲜的眼光。简单的眼光。

paras.en: I just saw this. And this is crazy. So here’s Xi’s number. So call Xi, maybe?
paras.zh: 我刚看到这个。这太疯狂了。所以这是 Xi 的号码。所以打给 Xi，也许？

paras.en: It’s hard to look right at this, baby. But yes, this happened. So call Xi, maybe.
paras.zh: 宝贝，直视这件事很难。但没错，这发生了。所以打给 Xi，也许。
